tool_input.command: set -a; . ~/.secrets; set +a; for i in $(seq 1 25); do out=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $BUILDKITE_ACCESS_TOKEN" "https://api.buildkite.com/v2/organizations/acme/pipelines/frontend/builds?branch=main&per_page=1" | python3 -c "import json,sys; b=json.load(sys.stdin)[0]; print(b['number'], b['state'], b['commit'][:8])"); echo "poll $i: $out"; case "$out" in *240868c0*passed*|*240868c0*failed*|*240868c0*blocked*) break;; esac; sleep 30; done
tool_input.description: Poll buildkite frontend build for commit 240868c0

provenance: Same command as postfail-genuine-partial-output, replayed as the PreToolUse call that should have been blocked before it ran (it predates the 2026-07-24 pretool hook). sleep 30 clears the threshold, so this looked like a clean catch-both case at first — but running it exposed a SEPARATE, more important bug found while building this eval: the loop-keyword bracket class `[;&|(\s]` does not mean 'preceded by whitespace' under real POSIX grep (confirmed on both /usr/bin/grep, BSD grep 2.6.0-FreeBSD, and by inspection GNU grep -E behaves the same — `\s` is only a whitespace shorthand under PCRE / grep -P, not inside an ERE bracket expression). It only matches if while/until/for sits at the very start of the command string or is directly adjacent (no space) to `;`, `&`, `|`, or `(`. This command has 'set +a; for i in ...' — a space between `;` and `for` — so the OLD hook misses it for a reason that has nothing to do with the sleep threshold. Minimal repro: printf '; for x in 1; do :; done' | grep -qE '(^|[;&|(\s])(while|until|for)[[:space:]]' → NOMATCH; a newline before 'for' (the common multi-line-script shape) also NOMATCH. Flagged to wp1-hooks-v2 directly since it's load-bearing for their rewrite.
